svg.title: Build the separate practice CA VM — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Build the separate practice CA VM
Your Windows 10 host · VMware Workstation Pro 17
VMware Workstation Pro 17 — Windows host
File Edit View VM Tabs Help
New Virtual Machine / Virtual Machine Settings
Name: TLS-CA01 Guest: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 64-bit
Memory: 2048 MB Processor: 1 processor / 1 core
Disk: 30 GB growable [ ] Allocate all disk space now
CD/DVD: your verified RHEL 9 x86_64 ISO
Temporary installation: NAT; later select Custom VMnet6
Next / Finish
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
VMware Library contains a new TLS-CA01 with its own RHEL 9 installation, learner account, one
vCPU, 2 GB RAM and growable 30 GB disk.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Create a second new VM named TLS-CA01 using the same VMware and RHEL installer steps. Use one vCPU, 2
GB RAM and a new 30 GB growable disk; use NAT only during installation.
2. Choose Minimal Install and create the same learner administrator account. Use tls-
ca01.lab.example.test as this VM’s hostname.
3. Finish the RHEL installer using the same Installation Summary choices from the application VM: new
virtual disk only, Minimal Install, adapter On, learner with administrator rights, then Begin
Installation and Reboot System.
4. At the text login prompt, sign in as learner. In the next step we will install the CA tools at this
separate VM’s console.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
